output.summary: Mirevanta Works begins with 3 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, 2 public Mandate, and CEO Owen Okafor. The Default Game runs through Eras I–IV, with three action cycles per Era. The institution with the most final Mandate wins; the shared World Ending is resolved separately.
rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed 13-tile map: Frontier at center, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. All setup pieces begin at Frontier; Frontier cannot be controlled and has no Facility spaces.

Use only Headline cards without the Advanced Play badge. Separate them by Era, shuffle each eligible deck, reveal three per Era, and leave resolved cards face up to form the twelve-card Future Timeline. Shuffle the Training deck and the three Mandate cards for each Era separately.

Place shared Runway, Compute, Safety, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Initiative, Audit bag, and Power Source components. Place each faction's Scrutiny cubes outside the bag. Record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of all factions' printed starting Trust.

Each faction starts with its CEO and one Team at Frontier, two Teams in supply, four Facilities, one Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, an AGI card, and its faction markers. Mirevanta's starting tracks are Runway 3, Compute 3, Capability 0, Customers 0, Trust 3, Safety 0, with 2 public Mandate.

Choose Initiative randomly. In each Era, the Era card readies all Core Actions, grants the stated Escalation availability, and provides three action cycles. Era I Progress grants no Escalation availability; Era II Capacity grants one; Era III Authority grants one; Era IV Continuity grants two.

At the start of each action cycle, reveal a Headline. Players secretly select one Core Action. Resolve players clockwise from Initiative: move zero, one, or two steps, then resolve the selected Action. Pass Initiative clockwise afterward. A later action can become blocked if an earlier player consumed every legal target; the later Action still exhausts without compensation.

Each player may make one complete resource offer to one rival immediately before or after Act. The rival may accept, reject, or publish one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. No redirects or further counteroffers occur. Runway, Compute, and Safety can be traded unless prohibited by the Headline.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny for Venture funding. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training; Build constructs a Facility or infrastructure; Organize recruits, redistributes Teams, or relocates a Facility; Deploy spends Compute to gain Customers when eligible; Influence handles Trust, Scrutiny, lobbying, and persistent agreements.

Research reveals Training cards. Each first ordinary domain gives provisional Capability; Mirevanta's seven domains are Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, and Synthetic. A successful stop banks provisional Capability. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing all provisional Capability and adding 1 Scrutiny. Safety or one Research Commons visit can protect a duplicate and immediately bank the current Capability; Mirevanta can instead pay 1 Runway for a protectable duplicate, once per Era. Synthetic Loop's first appearance is the unique Loop domain; its later duplicate is unprotectable.

Mirevanta may use Scaling-Law Breakthrough once per game during Research: each of the first three distinct domains banked grants 1 additional Capability, and the ability adds 2 Scrutiny. Peer Validation awards Mirevanta 1 Mandate at Capability 9 and 12, except that in a five-player game Capability 12 awards 2.

Movement crosses shared tile edges. CEOs and Teams have movement allowance up to two. Presence is CEO 2, Team 1, Facility 1; the highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex, with ties meaning no control. Facilities and Generators use local Power: a Generator powers Facilities on its own or adjacent hex, and Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Recalculate eligibility whenever pieces move or connections change.

Customers produce 1 Runway each during Production. Customer thresholds immediately award Mandate: Customers 1–3 award 2 each, and Customers 4–5 award 1 each. Resource caps are Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless a faction limit applies.

After the three action cycles, resolve Era Production and the Era's Mandate according to the unresolved timing rules. Era Mandates are revealed from the current Era deck; qualifying leaders score 2 Mandate, or 1 each for tied qualifying leaders. Ties use only the revealed Mandate's printed criterion.

Era IV activates Agent Swarms, AGI declarations, Fusion, Narrative Capture, and faction signature programs. Agent Swarm pairs two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both at the destination, applies the visit bonus to one, exhausts both, flips the card, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny unless a Headline/faction rule modifies it. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after complete demand is satisfied during completed Production.

Fusion requires ending movement on the Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, and having an available Generator slot. It occupies one of three shared slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, adds 3 Scrutiny, and does not count against the ordinary Generator-piece limit.

At each quarter, advance to the next Era, read its New this Era strip, reveal one of that Era's three Mandates and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era's Escalation availability. Exact placement of this step relative to final Production and Mandate scoring remains unresolved in the notes.

Final scoring reads all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud in Era order, then removes 1 Mandate for each offline Facility, never reducing a player below zero. No separate endgame Mandate is awarded for Facilities or control.

Resolve the shared World Ending using final AGI declarations, final Collective Trust, Setup Collective Trust, player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk cubes in the Audit bag. AGI emerges if a declaring institution finishes at Capability 9+. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count.

The World Ending is The Singularity for AGI plus Open, The Closed Loop for AGI plus Closed, The Plural Future for no AGI plus Open, and Assured Continuity for no AGI plus Closed. Read the corresponding World and Institutions narrative.
The highest-Mandate institution wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.

rulesReconstruction: Use Default Game only: exclude Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, Links, and Advanced-only effects.
Build the fixed 13-hex board: Frontier in the center; shuffle the six operational tiles within the inner ring and the six public tiles within the outer ring. All starting pieces begin at Frontier.

For seat 2, use Kestralyn: Jiwon Park as CEO; 6 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 starting public Mandate. Take three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, ten Scrutiny cubes, and the other faction components.

Prepare four three-card Era Mandate decks, Era-specific Default Headline decks, the Training deck, shared contract and risk components, the Audit bag, Initiative, and Power Source references. Establish Setup Collective Trust from the sum of printed starting Trust values.

Begin Era I with random Initiative. Each Era card is Progress, Capacity, Authority, or Continuity. At Era start, advance to the next Era, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate and box the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and grant that Era's Escalation availability.

Each Era contains three cycles. At each cycle start, reveal one eligible Headline into the current Future Timeline row. Then each player secretly selects one unused Core Action or spends Escalation availability to select one unlocked Escalation; reveal simultaneously.

Resolve players clockwise from Initiative. Each player selects a CEO or Team, moves it zero to two adjacent hexes, then resolves the committed Action from the destination. Exhaust the Core Action or flip the Escalation after resolution, then pass Initiative clockwise.

Selection is binding. If the committed Action becomes blocked, movement still occurs, the Action exhausts or Escalation flips, and it produces no compensation; do not rewind or replace it. Ties generally go to the tied player nearest Initiative clockwise.

Kestralyn's first Facility Build each Era costs one less Runway. If the discount actually reduces Runway paid for a completed Facility, Kestralyn scores one Mandate. Kestralyn's Orbital Compute may once per game move a Facility instead of the acting piece during movement, with attached components/designations, possible immediate production if presently powered, and two added Scrutiny.

Core Action summaries: Fund gains Runway; Research spends one Compute for a Training Run; Build constructs a Facility or, from Era II, a Generator; Organize recruits/moves Teams or relocates a Facility; Deploy spends one Compute for a Customer unless waived; Influence changes Trust/Scrutiny or creates/terminates a Joint Venture where permitted.

Research uses the 50-card Training deck. The first card from each ordinary domain grants one provisional Capability; an unprotected duplicate crashes the run. Safety or one Research Commons visit can protect one duplicate. Special cards include Curated Corpus, Benchmark Leak, Licensed Dataset, Synthetic Loop, and Human Evaluation. A successful run banks provisional Capability; discarded cards are reshuffled when the deck empties.

Build a Facility for two Runway in a non-Frontier hex with an open Facility space. Generators unlock in Era II, require Energy hexes, and are limited to one ordinary Generator per player and three shared slots per Energy hex. Facilities and Generators use local Power; offline Facilities remain present but produce nothing.

At the action window, one complete resource offer may be made to one rival. The rival accepts, rejects, or gives one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. No further negotiation or binding future promise is created.

After the three action cycles, run synchronized Production in Initiative order within each box: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, and Partner. Generate eligible local Power; permit at most one adjacent-rival Power purchase per player and at most one sale per supplier. Allocate available Power to legal Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Facilities receiving complete demand become Grid-Ready; insufficiently powered or relocated Grid-Ready Facilities revert to normal. Produce powered Facilities, Customers (one Runway each), and active Mega-Clusters. Partner produces active Joint Ventures.

Apply resource caps immediately: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless a printed faction exception applies. Add required Scrutiny to the Audit bag; if the player's ten-cube supply is exhausted, pay one Runway or lose one Trust, using the only available option.

Resolve the Era's Audit draw using the Era/player-count table. In Eras I–III, each drawn player cube costs its owner one Runway or one Trust. In Era IV, it costs two Runway or one Mandate. Drawn player cubes return to supply; undrawn cubes remain. Black Systemic Risk cubes apply the current Era penalty and return to supply.

Score the revealed Era Mandate using only its printed criterion. If nobody qualifies, score nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores two Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score one each. Keep the scored Mandate public beside the Era. Mandate awards are permanent and are not reversed by later losses.

Era IV additionally enables Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and faction signature programs. Agent Swarm resolves two different unused Core Actions from one destination and adds three Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least three Customers, three Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and three Compute; it scores seven Mandate for the first valid declaration and five thereafter, while adding three Scrutiny.
Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending five Runway. It occupies a Grid Generator slot, provides six Power, scores two Mandate, and adds three Scrutiny.

After Era IV's resolution, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud in Era order. Each player loses one Mandate per offline Facility, not below zero. Resolve the shared World Ending before announcing the winner.

Seat 3 plays Corthaven, led by Eli Rosen, with 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 starting public Mandate. rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed thirteen-tile map: Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. Frontier has no Facility spaces and cannot be controlled.

Place each CEO and one Team at Frontier. Corthaven’s CEO is Eli Rosen; its other two Teams remain in supply. Place each faction’s four Facilities, Generator, integrated starting-grid identifier, tracks, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, and starting resources according to its faction reference.
Set Corthaven to 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Award the printed starting Mandate once; do not rescore it later.
Set all ten Scrutiny cubes outside the Audit bag, leave the bag empty, and record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of printed starting Trust values.

Exclude Tactics, secret objectives, Links, Network production bonuses, Civic Permission Authority votes, and other Advanced Play procedures unless explicitly part of the Default Game rules. Use only eligible non-Advanced Headlines.

Prepare four three-card Era Mandate decks from the twelve Era Mandate cards and a twelve-card Future Timeline made from three eligible Headlines per Era. The exact selection and placement procedure is not supplied.

The Eras are Progress, Capacity, Authority, and Continuity. Each has three action cycles. At Era start, advance to the next fixed Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s deck, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability.

Progress has 0 Escalation availability and unlocks the basic Select → Move → Act loop, Training, starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Capacity adds 1 availability and unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Authority adds 1 and unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Continuity adds 2 and unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

At each cycle, reveal one Headline before secret action selection. Each player secretly chooses one unused Core Action or available Escalation, then all reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: move one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the selected Action from the destination. Blocked movement still exhausts or spends the selected Action without compensation. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

Corthaven’s Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training. Build costs 2 Runway for a Facility, or from Capacity onward builds an ordinary Generator on an Energy hex. Organize recruits or redistributes Teams, moves CEOs/Teams five total steps, or relocates one Facility for 1 Runway. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains the next Customer if the Capability requirement is met. Influence can gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or negotiate a Joint Venture from one of Corthaven’s Facilities.

During Capacity, once per cycle after the Headline and before action selection, Corthaven may use Allocation Window to create 2 temporary Compute. Each temporary token supports one restricted offer/counteroffer exchange; unused temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

During an active player’s negotiation window immediately before or after Act, they may make one complete resource offer to one rival. Only one counteroffer is allowed. Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged; accepted resources transfer immediately, promises are non-binding, and a Headline may prohibit a named resource.

Escalations are selected by spending one availability and are usable once per player per game. Corthaven’s listed Escalations include Mega-Cluster and Reorganization, but their exact Default availability and resolution details require confirmation.

After the three action cycles, Production is synchronized by box: Generate, Power Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. All players complete each box before the next box begins, with within-box resolution generally in Initiative order. Facilities must receive complete demand and legal Power to operate; after Production, qualifying normal Facilities become Grid-Ready. Grid-Ready Facilities immediately revert if relocated, lose Power eligibility, or receive insufficient Power.

Then resolve Public Audit using the Era’s Audit base—Progress 2, Capacity 3, Authority 4, Continuity 5—plus the missing Audit modifiers and timing rules. Scrutiny is represented by cubes in the Audit bag; removing Scrutiny returns that faction’s cubes from the bag to supply, as many as possible.

Resolve the revealed Era Mandate using its printed minimum qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, it scores nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Ties use only the revealed Mandate’s printed criterion, not resources, control, or public score. Keep scored Mandate cards face up as public history.

At Continuity, Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both Actions at the destination in either order, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, flips the Escalation, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. It is global after movement, scores 7 Mandate for the first declaration and 5 for later declarations, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Continuity-built Facilities cannot support a Continuity declaration.

Fusion requires ending movement on the Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway. It uses a Fusion marker in one of three Generator slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. It cannot be built if the corridor is full or all three slots are occupied.

At final scoring, read all twelve Timeline Headlines Era by Era. Subtract 1 Mandate for each offline Facility, without reducing a player below zero. Facilities and control provide no separate endgame Mandate.

Determine whether AGI emerged: at least one declaring institution must finish with Capability 9 or higher. Open requires Final Collective Trust at least Setup Collective Trust plus the player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk in the Audit bag lower than the player count. Both are required. AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity. Read the corresponding World Ending narrative, then announce the highest-Mandate institution and its claimed history. Ties break by higher Trust, more Customers, more Compute, then joint victory.

rulesReconstruction: Setup: Use the 13-tile board with Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. All CEOs and one Team per faction begin at Frontier; the other Teams remain in supply. Frontier has no Facility spaces and cannot be controlled.

Use only Default-eligible Headline cards. Shuffle the 50-card Training deck. Separate the twelve Era Mandates into four three-card Era decks. Set aside the shared contracts, Fusion marker, Initiative marker, Audit bag, Scrutiny cubes, and Power references.

Each player takes their faction board, CEO, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, Core Actions, Escalations, AGI card, and markers. Loopfold AI starts with Mateo Ibarra, 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate. Its Platform sequence begins at 1 Customer; its next Deploy requires 4 Capability.

Set each faction's printed starting tracks and public Mandate. Sum printed starting Trust values as Setup Collective Trust. Choose Initiative randomly; Initiative controls resolution order and unresolved ties, then passes clockwise after each cycle.

At the beginning of each Era, advance to that Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one of its three Mandates and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era's Escalation availability. Era I grants none; Era II grants one; Era III grants one; Era IV grants two. Unused availability expires at Era end, while unlocked and unused Escalations remain available.

Each Era contains three action cycles. At each cycle, reveal one Headline, secretly select one unused Core Action or one unlocked Escalation for which the player spends one availability, and reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative. For each committed selection: move one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the Action from the destination and apply applicable bonuses and modifiers. Exhaust selected Core Actions; flip used Escalations. Pass Initiative clockwise.

A committed Action is not replaced if it becomes blocked. If an earlier player consumed its target, it may resolve with no effect and still exhaust or spend the selection. A rejected or incomplete trade does not automatically cancel the Action; the exact no-legal-resolution fallback remains unclear.

Before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer to one rival involving Runway, Compute, or Safety. The rival accepts, rejects, or gives one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. There is no redirecting or further negotiation. Headlines may prohibit specified resources from trading.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. CEOs and Teams may act; Facilities and Generators cannot. Fund gives 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny through Venture funding. Research costs 1 Compute and runs the Training deck: provisional Capability is banked only on a successful bank; an unprotected duplicate crashes the run, discards provisional Capability, adds 1 Scrutiny, and ends the run. Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence require their detailed card procedures and map/power contracts.

Resource caps apply immediately: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3, subject to faction limits. Customers produce one Runway each during Production. Customer Mandate values are two each for Customers 1–3 and one each for Customers 4–5, with later Customers increasing public exposure. Capability, Trust, and Customer thresholds can permanently award Mandate as specified by the cards/rules.

Era II activates Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization. Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, adds 2 Scrutiny, requires an eligible Facility edge and 2 additional Power, and produces 3 Compute if powered; joint funding splits payments and yields 2 Compute to the lead and 1 to the partner if demand is met. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny.

Era III activates agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability, with an incomplete additional effect in the notes. Joint Ventures and immediate Power purchases become active.

Era IV activates Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and faction signature programs. Agent Swarm moves once, resolves two different unused Core Actions from the destination in either order, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI is global after movement and requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway; it occupies a Grid Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

During Production, Customers generate Runway and Facilities resolve their printed production if they receive complete demand. After Production, a Facility becomes Grid-Ready if it received complete demand. A Grid-Ready Facility immediately loses that status if relocated, loses legal Power eligibility, or receives insufficient Power. An Era-IV-built Facility cannot support an AGI declaration in that Era and must operate successfully in a later Production first.

End-of-Era Resolution: apply the Era's Production and Audit procedures using its Audit base, including Scrutiny handling and any Headline effects. Score the revealed Era Mandate only from its printed qualification: if nobody qualifies, score nothing; otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Keep scored Mandate cards beside the Era as public history. Advance to the next Era after resolving the current Era.

Final scoring: read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud, Era by Era. Subtract one Mandate for every offline Facility, without reducing a player below zero. Do not award separate endgame Mandate for Facilities, controlled hexes, stored resources, or unused cards.

Resolve the shared World Ending. AGI emerges if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk in the Audit bag is below player count. AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity.

The highest final Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then a joint victory with the specified merger announcement. Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, balance evidence, and duration evidence are excluded.

Presence is CEO 2, Team 1, Facility 1; the highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex, with ties meaning no control. Build a Facility for two Runway in a non-Frontier hex with an open Facility space. Generators unlock in Era II, require Energy hexes, and are limited to one ordinary Generator per player and three shared slots per Energy hex. Drawn player cubes return to supply; undrawn cubes remain. Black Systemic Risk cubes apply the current Era penalty and return to supply.

Score the revealed Era Mandate using only its printed criterion. If nobody qualifies, score nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores two Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score one each. Keep the scored Mandate public beside the Era. Mandate awards are permanent and are not reversed by later losses.

Era IV additionally enables Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and faction signature programs. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least three Customers, three Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and three Compute; it scores seven Mandate for the first valid declaration and five thereafter, while adding three Scrutiny.
Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending five Runway. It occupies a Grid Generator slot, provides six Power, scores two Mandate, and adds three Scrutiny.

After Era IV's resolution, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud in Era order. Each player loses one Mandate per offline Facility, not below zero. Resolve the shared World Ending before announcing the winner.

rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed thirteen-tile map: Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. Frontier has no Facility spaces and cannot be controlled.

Place each CEO and one Team at Frontier. Corthaven’s CEO is Eli Rosen; its other two Teams remain in supply. Place each faction’s four Facilities, Generator, integrated starting-grid identifier, tracks, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, and starting resources according to its faction reference.
Set Corthaven to 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Award the printed starting Mandate once; do not rescore it later.
Set all ten Scrutiny cubes outside the Audit bag, leave the bag empty, and record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of printed starting Trust values.

Exclude Tactics, secret objectives, Links, Network production bonuses, Civic Permission Authority votes, and other Advanced Play procedures unless explicitly part of the Default Game rules. Use only eligible non-Advanced Headlines.

Prepare four three-card Era Mandate decks from the twelve Era Mandate cards and a twelve-card Future Timeline made from three eligible Headlines per Era. The exact selection and placement procedure is not supplied.

The Eras are Progress, Capacity, Authority, and Continuity. Each has three action cycles. At Era start, advance to the next fixed Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s deck, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability.

Progress has 0 Escalation availability and unlocks the basic Select → Move → Act loop, Training, starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Capacity adds 1 availability and unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Authority adds 1 and unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Continuity adds 2 and unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

At each cycle, reveal one Headline before secret action selection. Each player secretly chooses one unused Core Action or available Escalation, then all reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: move one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the selected Action from the destination. Blocked movement still exhausts or spends the selected Action without compensation. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

Corthaven’s Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training. Build costs 2 Runway for a Facility, or from Capacity onward builds an ordinary Generator on an Energy hex. Organize recruits or redistributes Teams, moves CEOs/Teams five total steps, or relocates one Facility for 1 Runway. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains the next Customer if the Capability requirement is met. Influence can gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or negotiate a Joint Venture from one of Corthaven’s Facilities.

During Capacity, once per cycle after the Headline and before action selection, Corthaven may use Allocation Window to create 2 temporary Compute. Each temporary token supports one restricted offer/counteroffer exchange; unused temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

During an active player’s negotiation window immediately before or after Act, they may make one complete resource offer to one rival. Only one counteroffer is allowed. Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged; accepted resources transfer immediately, promises are non-binding, and a Headline may prohibit a named resource.

Escalations are selected by spending one availability and are usable once per player per game. Corthaven’s listed Escalations include Mega-Cluster and Reorganization, but their exact Default availability and resolution details require confirmation.

After the three action cycles, Production is synchronized by box: Generate, Power Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. All players complete each box before the next box begins, with within-box resolution generally in Initiative order. Facilities must receive complete demand and legal Power to operate; after Production, qualifying normal Facilities become Grid-Ready. Grid-Ready Facilities immediately revert if relocated, lose Power eligibility, or receive insufficient Power.

Then resolve Public Audit using the Era’s Audit base—Progress 2, Capacity 3, Authority 4, Continuity 5—plus the missing Audit modifiers and timing rules. Scrutiny is represented by cubes in the Audit bag; removing Scrutiny returns that faction’s cubes from the bag to supply, as many as possible.

Resolve the revealed Era Mandate using its printed minimum qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, it scores nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Ties use only the revealed Mandate’s printed criterion, not resources, control, or public score. Keep scored Mandate cards face up as public history.

At Continuity, Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both Actions at the destination in either order, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, flips the Escalation, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. It is global after movement, scores 7 Mandate for the first declaration and 5 for later declarations, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Continuity-built Facilities cannot support a Continuity declaration.

Fusion requires ending movement on the Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway. It uses a Fusion marker in one of three Generator slots, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. It cannot be built if the corridor is full or all three slots are occupied.

At final scoring, read all twelve Timeline Headlines Era by Era. Subtract 1 Mandate for each offline Facility, without reducing a player below zero. Facilities and control provide no separate endgame Mandate.

Determine whether AGI emerged: at least one declaring institution must finish with Capability 9 or higher. Open requires Final Collective Trust at least Setup Collective Trust plus the player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk in the Audit bag lower than the player count. Both are required. AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity. Read the corresponding World Ending narrative, then announce the highest-Mandate institution and its claimed history. Ties break by higher Trust, more Customers, more Compute, then joint victory.

rulesReconstruction: Setup: Use the 13-tile board with Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. All CEOs and one Team per faction begin at Frontier; the other Teams remain in supply. Frontier has no Facility spaces and cannot be controlled.

Use only Default-eligible Headline cards. Shuffle the 50-card Training deck. Separate the twelve Era Mandates into four three-card Era decks. Set aside the shared contracts, Fusion marker, Initiative marker, Audit bag, Scrutiny cubes, and Power references.

Loopfold AI starts with Mateo Ibarra, 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate. Its Platform sequence begins at 1 Customer; its next Deploy requires 4 Capability.

Set each faction's printed starting tracks and public Mandate. Sum printed starting Trust values as Setup Collective Trust. Choose Initiative randomly; Initiative controls resolution order and unresolved ties, then passes clockwise after each cycle.

At the beginning of each Era, advance to that Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one of its three Mandates and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era's Escalation availability. Era I grants none; Era II grants one; Era III grants one; Era IV grants two. Unused availability expires at Era end, while unlocked and unused Escalations remain available.

Each Era contains three action cycles. At each cycle, reveal one Headline, secretly select one unused Core Action or one unlocked Escalation for which the player spends one availability, and reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative. For each committed selection: move one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the Action from the destination and apply applicable bonuses and modifiers. Exhaust selected Core Actions; flip used Escalations. Pass Initiative clockwise.

A committed Action is not replaced if it becomes blocked. If an earlier player consumed its target, it may resolve with no effect and still exhaust or spend the selection. A rejected or incomplete trade does not automatically cancel the Action; the exact no-legal-resolution fallback remains unclear.

Before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer to one rival involving Runway, Compute, or Safety. The rival accepts, rejects, or gives one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects. There is no redirecting or further negotiation. Headlines may prohibit specified resources from trading.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. CEOs and Teams may act; Facilities and Generators cannot. Fund gives 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny through Venture funding. Research costs 1 Compute and runs the Training deck: provisional Capability is banked only on a successful bank; an unprotected duplicate crashes the run, discards provisional Capability, adds 1 Scrutiny, and ends the run. Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence require their detailed card procedures and map/power contracts.

Resource caps apply immediately: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3, subject to faction limits. Customers produce one Runway each during Production. Customer Mandate values are two each for Customers 1–3 and one each for Customers 4–5, with later Customers increasing public exposure. Capability, Trust, and Customer thresholds can permanently award Mandate as specified by the cards/rules.

Era II activates Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization. Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, adds 2 Scrutiny, requires an eligible Facility edge and 2 additional Power, and produces 3 Compute if powered; joint funding splits payments and yields 2 Compute to the lead and 1 to the partner if demand is met. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny.

Era III activates agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability, with an incomplete additional effect in the notes. Joint Ventures and immediate Power purchases become active.

Era IV activates Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and faction signature programs. Agent Swarm moves once, resolves two different unused Core Actions from the destination in either order, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI is global after movement and requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway; it occupies a Grid Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

During Production, Customers generate Runway and Facilities resolve their printed production if they receive complete demand. After Production, a Facility becomes Grid-Ready if it received complete demand. A Grid-Ready Facility immediately loses that status if relocated, loses legal Power eligibility, or receives insufficient Power. An Era-IV-built Facility cannot support an AGI declaration in that Era and must operate successfully in a later Production first.

End-of-Era Resolution: apply the Era's Production and Audit procedures using its Audit base, including Scrutiny handling and any Headline effects. Score the revealed Era Mandate only from its printed qualification: if nobody qualifies, score nothing; otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Keep scored Mandate cards beside the Era as public history. Advance to the next Era after resolving the current Era.

Final scoring: read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud, Era by Era. Subtract one Mandate for every offline Facility, without reducing a player below zero. Do not award separate endgame Mandate for Facilities, controlled hexes, stored resources, or unused cards.

Resolve the shared World Ending. AGI emerges if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk in the Audit bag is below player count. AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity.

The highest final Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then a joint victory with the specified merger announcement. Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, balance evidence, and duration evidence are excluded.

findings.evidence: The jurisdiction uses thirteen tiles in a sixfold-symmetric layout. Frontier is central and has no Facility spaces. Every other hex has two Facility spaces. Every piece placed during setup begins at Frontier. The Power Corridor is one of the six operational-ring tiles; one movement step crosses one shared tile edge, and movement is up to two steps.

findings.evidence: Each faction has four double-sided Facilities (normal/Grid-Ready) and one Generator. After Production, flip a Facility to Grid-Ready if it received its complete Facility demand. Flip it back immediately if relocated, if it becomes ineligible for its owner’s Power, or if it receives insufficient Power during Production. Power offline recovery is reassessed every Production.

findings.evidence: The printed Escalation texts are: Mega-Cluster—spend 3 Runway and 2 Compute; construction may be joint-funded; rejection, pass, or no response ends the attempt and uses the Escalation; it demands 2 Power, produces 3 Compute, and adds 2 Scrutiny. Reorganization—move every Team up to one hex; optionally return one for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny; does not ready or resolve another Action. Open Weights—everyone gains 1 Capability; you gain 2 Trust and remove 1 Scrutiny. Narrative Capture—remove 2 Scrutiny, gain 2 Runway, or add 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers. Agent Swarm—resolve two different unused Core Actions, exhaust both, add 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI—if eligible, spend 3 Compute, score the declaration Mandate, and add 3 Scrutiny; the game continues. Fusion Demonstrator—on Power Corridor, spend 5 Runway to construct 6 Power, score 2 Mandate, and add 3 Scrutiny. Each is once per player per game, and selecting an unlocked card spends one Escalation availability. Era-specific availability is not stated here.

findings.evidence: Open Weights is an Escalation card. Every player gains 1 Capability; the acting player gains 2 Trust and removes 1 Scrutiny. It is selected as an unlocked Escalation and is once per player per game. No further timing detail is provided.

Person: Declare AGI requires Trust 4, scores 2 additional Mandate, and removes 1 Scrutiny from that declaring player whenever a declaration resolves. findings.evidence: The Era Mandate is revealed from the current Era’s deck. If nobody meets its minimum qualification, nobody scores; otherwise the leader scores 2 Mandate and tied leaders score 1 each. Listed criteria include most Capability gained, broadest Training Run, most Fund Runway, most powered Facilities, most satisfied Power demand, most Compute produced, most active new Joint Ventures, most Trust among Deploying players, most hex categories controlled, most Customers gained, fewest Scrutiny added among players adding Scrutiny, and most Capability among players with at least 4 Trust.
